summary: Fourteen governments whose travel advice we read, among them the UK, Ireland, Canada, France, Germany and Spain, tell their own citizens that they need a visa for Guinea-Bissau, and Portugal's says its citizens need an entry authorisation; Singapore's says Singaporeans get a visa on arrival. Germany's foreign ministry says a visa is also issued at Bissau airport, but not at land borders. ECOWAS citizens enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol.

payments.text: The UK government describes Guinea-Bissau as a cash-based economy where credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs; Canada's travel advice says there are no ATMs. Canada adds that foreign currency can be brought in without limit if declared on arrival, and that taking it out is limited to the amount declared.

safety.text: The UK says Guinea-Bissau suffers from political instability and advises avoiding sensitive areas such as military installations and government buildings. It says pickpocketing and bag and phone snatching are relatively common in Bissau, and that landmines remain a risk in parts of the country: outside Bissau, take local advice and stay on paved roads.

Canada's travel advice says the Bijagós Islands are reached by chartered air services or by boat, that tour operators organise boat trips, and that pirogues should be avoided because they are unsafe.

The UK government says credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are none. Canada also says local currency may not be imported or exported, while foreign currency must be declared on arrival.

Canada's travel advice says the army seized power on 26 November 2025, after the presidential election, and formed a transitional government. The UK government advises avoiding sensitive areas such as military installations and government buildings and following local authorities during any unrest.
Poland's foreign ministry names rgb-visa.com as the place to apply for a Guinea-Bissau visa online, and Spain's says the online application has stopped working.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport, and for most passports no official source we could read states the rule. The governments of the UK, Ireland, Canada, France, Germany, Spain and eight others tell their own citizens that they need a visa; Ireland's foreign ministry says Irish citizens apply in person at a Guinea-Bissau mission such as the embassy in Paris or Lisbon and pay EUR 70 for 45 days, EUR 110 for 90 days or EUR 200 for 180 days. Singapore's foreign ministry says Singaporeans get a visa on arrival for up to 90 days. ECOWAS citizens are exempt and enter freely under the bloc's free-movement protocol, as for now are citizens of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which left ECOWAS in January 2025.

faq.question: How does the visa on arrival in Guinea-Bissau work?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a visa on arrival open to every passport. Germany's foreign ministry says German citizens can get one at Bissau airport (EUR 80 for 30 days) but not at a land border, and still tells them to apply in advance at Guinea-Bissau's embassy in Brussels. France's says an airport visa is possible when your contact in Guinea-Bissau has told the immigration department in advance, in an emergency, or when your country of departure has no Guinea-Bissau embassy or consulate, and that it is paid in cash. China's says the visa on arrival has to be applied for in advance to Guinea-Bissau's Directorate of Migration and Borders, and Singapore's says Singaporeans may stay up to 90 days with a visa issued on arrival.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: Yes, according to the UK Foreign Office: you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination to enter Guinea-Bissau.

faq.question: Is Guinea-Bissau safe to visit?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says to exercise a high degree of caution because of high crime rates and weak state infrastructure, that the army seized power on 26 November 2025, that petty crime, including pickpocketing, is common at the airport, in markets and at public gatherings, and that even peaceful demonstrations can turn violent.

faq.question: Can I pay by card in Guinea-Bissau?
faq.answer: The UK government says Guinea-Bissau is a cash-based economy where credit cards are rarely used and there are not many ATMs, and Canada says there are no ATMs at all. Canada also says foreign currency must be declared on arrival.
